title: Conjecture 1.3 (Conlon, Fox, Sudakov) / Sparse Linear Conjecture
statement_text: For every graph $H$ there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ with $|G| > 1$ contains a pure $(\varepsilon|G|, \varepsilon|G|)$-pair.
context_text: Stated as problem 3.13 in [4], this asserts that every $H$-free graph contains two disjoint sets of linear size that are either completely joined or anticomplete. It is equivalent to Conjecture 1.4 (the sparse linear conjecture) via a theorem of Rödl. The sparse linear conjecture form states that either some vertex has degree at least $\varepsilon|G|$, or there are two disjoint anticomplete sets of sizes at least $\varepsilon|G|^\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon|G|$.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for all almost-bipartite graphs $H$ (triangle-free graphs whose vertex set partitions into a stable set and a set inducing a graph of maximum degree at most one); in particular establishes it for the four-cycle and its complement.

title: Conjecture 1.4
statement_text: For every graph $H$ there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that in every $H$-free $\varepsilon$-bounded graph $G$ with $|G| > 1$ vertices, there is an anticomplete $(\varepsilon|G|^{\varepsilon}, \varepsilon|G|)$-pair.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple, $|G|$ is the number of vertices, and $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph is isomorphic to $H$. $G$ is $\varepsilon$-bounded if $|N[v]|<\varepsilon|G|$ for every vertex $v$ (closed neighbourhood), i.e. maximum degree less than $\varepsilon|G|-1$. An $(x,y)$-pair is a pair $(A,B)$ of disjoint vertex sets with $|A|\ge x$ and $|B|\ge y$; it is anticomplete if there is no edge between $A$ and $B$, pure if it is complete or anticomplete, $c$-sparse if there are at most $c|A||B|$ edges between $A$ and $B$, and $c$-dense if there are at least $c|A||B|$. Conlon, Fox and Sudakov conjectured that for every $H$ there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ with $|G|>1$ contains a pure $(\varepsilon|G|^\varepsilon,\varepsilon|G|)$-pair (one side linear); in an $\varepsilon$-bounded graph no such pair can be complete, so this implies the sparse linear conjecture: for every $H$ there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that every $H$-free $\varepsilon$-bounded graph $G$ with $|G|>1$ has an anticomplete $(\varepsilon|G|^\varepsilon,\varepsilon|G|)$-pair. By a theorem of Rödl, $H$ satisfies the first conjecture if and only if both $H$ and $\overline{H}$ satisfy the second, so the two are equivalent over all $H$, though the second is much more tractable for particular $H$. A graph $H$ is almost-bipartite if it is triangle-free and its vertex set can be partitioned into a stable set and a set inducing a subgraph of maximum degree at most one (e.g. any graph in which every edge of another graph is subdivided at least once). The authors' main result is that every almost-bipartite $H$ satisfies the sparse linear conjecture; as a consequence the first conjecture also holds for $C_4$ and its complement. The case $H=K_3$ remains open.

title: Conjecture 3.3 (Conlon, Fox, Sudakov)
statement_text: For every graph $H$ there exist $\varepsilon, s > 0$ such that for every $H$-free graph $G$ with $|G| > 1$, and every $c$ with $0 \leq c \leq 1$, $G$ contains either a $c$-sparse or a $(1-c)$-dense $(\varepsilon c^s |G|,\, \varepsilon|G|)$-pair.
context_text: This strengthens the density theorem 3.2 of Erdős–Hajnal by requiring one of the two sets to have size linear in $|G|$, independent of $c$. It is attributed to Conlon, Sudakov, and Fox (problem 3.13 in [4]) and implies Conjecture 1.3. A pair $(A,B)$ is $c$-sparse if $|E(A,B)| \leq c|A||B|$ and $(1-c)$-dense if $|E(A,B)| \geq (1-c)|A||B|$.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for all almost-bipartite graphs $H$ as a consequence of the main theorem (Theorem 4.5).

title: Conjecture 3.4
statement_text: For every graph $H$ there exist $\varepsilon, s > 0$ such that for every $H$-free $\varepsilon$-bounded graph $G$ with $|G| > 1$, and every $c$ with $0 \leq c \leq 1$, there is a $c$-sparse $(\varepsilon c^s |G|,\, \varepsilon|G|)$-pair in $G$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple, $|G|$ is the number of vertices, and $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph is isomorphic to $H$. $G$ is $\varepsilon$-bounded if $|N[v]|<\varepsilon|G|$ for every vertex $v$ (closed neighbourhood), i.e. maximum degree less than $\varepsilon|G|-1$. An $(x,y)$-pair is a pair $(A,B)$ of disjoint vertex sets with $|A|\ge x$ and $|B|\ge y$; it is anticomplete if there is no edge between $A$ and $B$, pure if it is complete or anticomplete, $c$-sparse if there are at most $c|A||B|$ edges between $A$ and $B$, and $c$-dense if there are at least $c|A||B|$. Erdős and Hajnal proved that for every $H$ there are $\varepsilon,s>0$ such that every $H$-free $G$ with $|G|>1$ contains, for every $0\le c\le1$, a $c$-sparse or a $(1-c)$-dense $(\varepsilon c^s|G|,\varepsilon c^s|G|)$-pair, a key step towards their bound $2^{\varepsilon\sqrt{\log|G|}}$ on cliques or stable sets. Conlon, Fox and Sudakov asked whether one side can be made linear, i.e. a $c$-sparse or $(1-c)$-dense $(\varepsilon c^s|G|,\varepsilon|G|)$-pair; in $\varepsilon$-bounded graphs the dense outcome is impossible, which gives this conjecture. The authors note the implications: the Conlon–Fox–Sudakov question implies this conjecture, which in turn implies the sparse linear conjecture (every $H$-free $\varepsilon$-bounded graph with $|G|>1$ has an anticomplete $(\varepsilon|G|^\varepsilon,\varepsilon|G|)$-pair). For almost-bipartite $H$ (triangle-free, with vertex set partitioned into a stable set and a set inducing maximum degree at most one) they prove a stronger statement: there are $\varepsilon,t>0$ such that every graph $G$ with $|G|>1$ and maximum degree less than $\varepsilon|G|$ contains, for every $0<c\le1$, either $\varepsilon c^t|G|^{|H|}$ induced copies of $H$ or a pair $A,B$ with $|A|\ge\varepsilon c^t|G|$, $|B|\ge\varepsilon|G|$ and at most $c|A||B|$ edges between them; in particular this conjecture holds for almost-bipartite $H$.

title: Conjecture 4.3
statement_text: For every graph $H$ there exist $\varepsilon, s > 0$ such that for every graph $G$ with $|G| > 1$, and all $c$ with $0 \leq c \leq 1$, either $G$ is $(\varepsilon c^s, H)$-saturated, or there is a $c$-sparse or $(1-c)$-dense $(\varepsilon c^s |G|,\, \varepsilon|G|)$-pair in $G$.
context_text: A saturation strengthening of Conjecture 3.3: instead of requiring $G$ to be $H$-free, one only needs $G$ to not be $(\varepsilon c^s, H)$-saturated (i.e., to contain fewer than $\varepsilon c^s |G|^{|H|}$ induced copies of $H$). The implications $4.3 \Rightarrow 3.3$ and $4.3 \Rightarrow 4.4$ hold.

title: Conjecture 4.4
statement_text: For every graph $H$ there exist $\varepsilon, s > 0$ such that for every $\varepsilon$-bounded graph $G$ and all $c$ with $0 \leq c \leq 1$, either $G$ is $(\varepsilon c^s, H)$-saturated, or there is a $c$-sparse $(\varepsilon c^s |G|,\, \varepsilon|G|)$-pair in $G$.
context_text: This is the saturation strengthening of Conjecture 3.4 and the $\varepsilon$-bounded specialisation of Conjecture 4.3. The paper proves this conjecture for all almost-bipartite graphs $H$ (Theorem 4.5), and shows that it becomes false if the $(\varepsilon c^s, H)$-saturation threshold is weakened to $\varepsilon$-saturation.
